quality.testing.summary: 39 backend pytest + 6 frontend vitest tests, all passing, cover the auto_finder fix, record_observation write-back/dead-link/conflict logic, and ListingUrl's verified/unverified/dead states plus an XSS guard.

quality.observability.summary: No new logs/metrics/dashboards added or required.
quality.observability.rationale: The acceptance criteria for N-0039 are about URL correctness and link-state presentation, not diagnosability; existing parse_flags diagnostic fields (fetch_reason, details_status) were preserved incidentally but there is no new observability surface to assess.

quality.ux.summary: UI now distinguishes verified (real anchor + verification-time tooltip), unverified (plain text + explanatory tooltip), and dead (plain text + Dead link) instead of presenting every stored URL as an equally trustworthy plain string.

quality.a11y.summary: Verified links render as real focusable <a> via MUI Link; non-link states use Tooltip-wrapped span plus a text-labeled StatusChip, so the distinction does not rely on color alone.

quality.rendered.summary: Live-rendered and inspected Takealot listing 65 in the running app: stored bare-PLID URL shown as non-clickable plain text with an Unverified link chip. Verified-anchor state for a non-Takealot listing was not independently rendered live within tool budget (see limitations).

quality.content.summary: "Unverified link" / "Dead link" labels and tooltip copy are plain, non-alarming, and correctly scoped to link verification state rather than listing status.

verification.rendered.summary: Independent live render performed in this GOV-008 session (separate run from implementation) against the running app and real cip data, confirming the Takealot unverified/non-anchor behavior end-to-end.

verification.referent.summary: All cited commit hashes (fc69fda3, b17e950, bfd0c44), file:line evidence, and read-only SQL against cip are independently reproducible; re-ran the SQL and test commands myself this session.

limitations: Takealot URL-shape routing behavior (/PLID<n> -> seo-landing vs /x/PLID<n> -> product page) is ASSERTED from DISCOVERY.md's own rate-limited sample GETs, not independently reproduced over the network by this review.

The verified (real, clickable anchor) link state was confirmed via passing unit tests, code review, and a matching read-only SQL row in cip (listing id 1, amazon), not via a live click-through in Chrome, due to ag-Grid/customer-filter UI friction within the review's tool budget.
